title: Africa Aims to Transform The Continent Inspired By Asia’s Rise
content:
By Kalinga Seneviratne

BANGKOK, Thailand | 21 October 2026 (IDN) — The IMF-World Bank annual meeting returned to Bangkok last week (12 to 18 October) after more than three decades, with nervous Thai authorities going to great lengths to stem any disruptions to it by civil society protests.

Inside Bangkok’s convention center, World Bank’s turbaned American-Sikh President Ajay Banga led a charm offensive to convince the world that the Bank is transforming the development model of previous generations to one that addresses the expectations of equality among nations. He even talked about building models that develop local industries that create local jobs and keep the value of their natural resources at home. He even launched a Philanthropy Hub in Bangkok, which the Bank claims will take them in a direction of more partnerships with a variety of stakeholders.

title: Israel’s Fateful Election: A Nation On The Brink
content:
Israel’s next election will decide far more than who governs. It will help determine whether the country can reclaim its democratic foundations, restore its international standing, and fulfil its founding promise—or continue down a path that endangers the very future its leaders claim to defend.

By Alon Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — Hardly any election in Israel’s history has carried such profound consequences. Israelis will face a choice that reaches far beyond party allegiance: what kind of country will they leave their children? After 7 October and three years of devastating wars, Israel’s security, democratic character, and promise as a Jewish homeland demand an unsparing national reckoning—one that confronts democratic erosion through judicial subversion, institutional capture, press intimidation, dissent suppression, minority disenfranchisement, unchecked executive power, perpetual warfare, and isolation.

title: Decoding Pro-Israel Buzzwords in a Time of Genocide
content:
By Norman Solomon*

SAN FRANCISCO | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — Nearly two years ago, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International released in-depth reports documenting that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Months later, Israeli human rights groups did likewise. Support for Israel has declined steeply among Americans, but its defenders continue to maintain a siege of buzzwords against Palestinian rights.

As historian Rashid Khalidi emphasized in his book Brokers of Deceit: How the U.S. Has Undermined Peace in the Middle East, “language matters.” Standard terms and tropes “are the essential building blocks of a lofty and solid edifice of denial of an entire narrative, of the existence of an entire people, which is basic to the affirmation of a formidable counterreality.”

Prominent groups, notably the Anti-Defamation League, the American Jewish Committee, AIPAC and Christians United for Israel – along with allies in Congress, the Executive Branch and the punditocracy – rely on the same buzzwords to defame critics of Israel and deny its systematic crimes against Palestinian people. title: Hunger Amid Plenty Is a Political Failure, UN Rights Chief Warns
content:
The world produces more than enough food, yet conflict, inequality, waste and the concentration of farmland leave billions without an adequate diet.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — The world’s farms produce more food than ever before. The average global supply now exceeds 3,000 calories per person a day. Yet more than a quarter of humanity cannot regularly obtain enough food—or food of sufficient quality—to live a healthy life.

For UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk, this contradiction makes hunger more than a humanitarian emergency. It is evidence of economic and political systems that fail to distribute the world’s abundance fairly.

Addressing the UN-hosted Committee on World Food Security in Rome on 19 October, Türk described hunger as an avoidable tragedy. The international community, he argued, already possesses the food, knowledge and resources needed to prevent it.

What is missing is the political determination to make the right to food a reality.

The scale of global food production challenges the long-standing assumption that hunger is mainly caused by shortages.

title: Germany’s Colonial Reckoning Returns to the Bundestag
content:
Debate over the genocide committed in Namibia has revived questions about recognition, reparations and whether Germany is willing to confront its colonial past as seriously as other chapters of its history.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — Over a century after German colonial troops committed mass killings in what is now Namibia, the subject has resurfaced in the Bundestag with significant political momentum.

The whole thing was kicked off by an opposition motion calling for Germany to recognise the genocide against the Ovaherero and Nama unambiguously and to go beyond development aid to what the proponents would describe as restorative justice. DW reported on the ensuing parliamentary debate and the long-standing dispute over recognition and reparations.

title: Decline of European Culture: Decadence, Hatred, and Incitement
content:
A commentary by Wolfgang Bittner*

GÖTTINGEN, Germany | 19 October 2026 (IDN) — Russia is to be defeated—at any cost. The Berlin government intends to continue supporting Ukraine in its war with weapons and funds at the expense of its own population, “for as long as necessary.” [1]

It is questionable how much longer this can go on. But in this situation, there is an opportunity to break free from vassalage and the US’s military and cultural stranglehold and rediscover one’s own cultural roots. The primary objective should be to establish Germany’s sovereignty and neutrality, which would allow many current problems to be resolved. This requires a fundamental policy shift.

With respect to the war in Ukraine, it is becoming increasingly clear that this is not merely a conflict between the Collective West and the Global South, including Russia, but, in the broadest sense, a clash between two cultural spheres: the decadent US-dominated Western culture and a historically grown conservative European culture.

title: Offshore Borders: Inside EU’s Ultimate Migration Strategy
content:
By Francesca Lonardoni

BRUSSELS, Belgium | 19 October 2026 (IDN) — Externalising the European Union’s (EU) borders has become a central priority in European migration policy. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s 2026 State of the European Union address to the European Parliament confirmed this trend, which has been developing for years. Referring directly to the recent Ceuta migration crisis of July 2026, von der Leyen emphasised the need to fully implement the Pact on Migration and Asylum and deepen collaboration with third-partner countries.

title: EEPA Reports on New Caretaker Administration Appointed in Tigray
content:
BRUSSELS | 19 October 2026 (IDN | EEPA) — The following are the situation reports on the situation in Ethiopia, the situation in Sudan, the regional and international situation, new Caretaker Administration appointed in Tigray, ENDF and TPF recapture Aksum, 11 killed in RSF attack on IDP camp in West Darfur

  • The Federal Government established a caretaker administration for the Tigray Regional State on 16 October to administer the region for six months. Its main tasks include organising elections, facilitating the return of internally displaced persons (IDPs), and restoring security and peace in the region. 
  • The appointed senior officials of the administration are Asefa Abraha Hagos (administration), Tewodros Aregay (economy), Brig. Gen. Gebre-Egziabher Beyene (security and peace), Redae Halefom (political affairs) and Shishay Amare (Mekelle mayor).
  • The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) firmly rejected the new caretaker administration, defining it as an “illegitimate political structure” and warning local institutions not to collaborate with it.

title: Regional Trade and Economic Strategy Draw Asia and Africa Closer to BRICS
content:
By Professor Maurice Okoli, Ph.D*

This article was first published in Eurasia Review.

MOSCOW | 17 October 2026 (IDN) — Perhaps, BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa), with the new members and partner states, summit in New Delhi, from 11 September to 13, produced a new round of significant declarations, adapting its collective policy toward an increasingly emerging architecture, while distinctively building an ‘Asian model’ of economic alliance. Under India’s chairmanship, the summit focused on building a reputation that has been developing for nearly two decades. The timing was, particularly, notable. The most important strategic message was coined: “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability.”

title: The Narcissist In Chief
content:
By Alon Ben-Meir*

When a president confuses personal loyalty with public duty and self-glorification with leadership, democracy pays the price. Trump’s conduct reveals a disgusting and disturbing pattern: he put the presidency in service of his ego rather than the nation.

NEW YORK | 17 October 2026 (IDN) — The damage Trump has inflicted on this country and the world is incalculable. The irony is staggering: he emerged from the very America that led the world order after the Second World War. He has repeatedly inverted that obligation, treating public office as a platform for self-glorification, a tool for retaliation, and a means of demanding personal loyalty, at a time when the US presidency, in particular, demands judgment, restraint, and a commitment to something greater than oneself.

title: EEPA reports on deadly drone strike on Abyei market
content:

  • An Ethiopian National Defence Force (ENDF) jet flew over Mekele in the morning of 21 October, according to an ACLED report. Tigray Television claimed that there was no military threat to residents. 
  • The ENDF retook control of Nirak, Abergele woreda’s administrative center, in Amhara, after the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) forces had taken control of the place on 19 October. 
  • The TPLF forces claimed to have killed 1,511 ENDF soldiers and many others injured in a surprise attack near Merena, central Tigray, during an attempted advance towards Adet, on 19 October. 
  • Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has issued a strong warning to Eritrea of “very severe” consequences for allegedly supporting groups, such as the TPLF, that aim to destabilise Ethiopia.
